calls.reason: The claim has no deadline and names no metric. The only evidence is that METR stopped updating its time-horizon page in September 2026, which measures nothing about whether AI progress has stopped doubling.
The only support is Naam's own unverified normalization. A LessWrong analysis flags possible errors in it, and the packet has no public Epoch ECI score for Mythos and no trend fit.

METR's own January 2026 note says a 50% time horizon does not mean tasks of that length can be delegated to AI. Its graph also covers only technical software tasks, so it cannot show reliable performance on most human activities.

Marcus frames this as a strong intuition, which is hedged. No authenticated Remote Labor Index score for Mythos Preview was found, and Anthropic's robotics study shows some physical-task gains without measuring whole jobs.

There is no deadline, and the evidence shows only that METR's benchmark is saturated, which is a measurement limit. Nothing in the packet shows either a lasting ceiling or the threshold being reached.
